| D-45 | The S5 write stage has ONE implemented shape: binary `open(path, "wb")` (write, flush) with D-43's encode-before-open order; a text-mode build (`open(path, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8")`, writing `document` itself) is NON-CONFORMING for this stage — its encode runs implicitly INSIDE the write call, necessarily AFTER the open has applied O_TRUNC, so a MemoryError at that implicit encode destroys a pre-existing output (the exact D-43 destruction class; adv-c5 probe P1: text-mode shape truncates/removes the prior file, binary shape byte-identical on the identical fault; re-verified as R6-P1 in appendix/28-rev6-writegate-probes.py) and the pre-open no-side-effect phase QC-2 relies on cannot exist in that shape; closes adv-c5 F-01 (the v5 "Equivalent conforming alternative" parenthetical is deleted) (spec/06-spec-v6.md §4.5, §5.3 S-14, QC-2, §8.3 T-C8/T-C16) | DECIDED | spec-designer | spec/06-spec-v6.md §4.5, §10 QC-2 |

| D-47 | Aliasing boundary for the D-33 compensation: the compensation's unit of mutation is the opened NAME (best-effort `os.remove` of the exact opened path, never an inode-directed truncation) while the write's unit of mutation is the targeted INODE — under a symlink/hardlink output path, open() writes THROUGH the link and a failed post-open run can leave the partial payload in the aliased real/twin file while the opened name is removed (adv-c5 probes P2/P2b; re-verified as R6-P5); disposition accepted-risk (a) per adv-c5 F-02's own options — recorded as R-1b in spec §10.1 (owner, rationale, impact, mitigation, verification) and documented assert-or-accept in T-C8's matrix; tightening the mechanism (create-then-rename, fd-based unlink) was rejected because it adds temp-file machinery ADR-4 designed out and no REQ covers aliased targets (spec/06-spec-v6.md §4.5, §10.1 R-1b, §8.3 T-C8) | DECIDED | spec-designer | spec/06-spec-v6.md §4.5, §10.1 |
| D-48 | The D-33 compensation's REFERENCE SHAPE is except-scoped: the best-effort `os.remove(path)` lives in the failure arm ONLY — guarded by whether the open SUCCEEDED (`fd is not None`), with the arm re-raising so §4.5's propagation rules are unchanged — and the success path closes the fd and can never run the remove; a finally-based shape conforms ONLY with an explicit failure flag set at try entry and cleared after the close (the remove firing only while the flag still reads True); the v6 try/finally snippet (`fd = None; try: fd = open(...); ... finally: if fd is not None: remove(path)`) is superseded — its finally runs on the SUCCESS path too (fd is not None after a successful open), deleting every successful run's just-written output (adv-c6 probe P1), and it never closed the fd (adv-c6 probe P1b: the except-scoped shape keeps the file on success and removes it on failure, satisfying the normative state contract); v8 REFRESH (SR6-F-01/F-02, closes SR6-F-01): the failure arm now CLOSES the fd (best-effort, errors ignored) BEFORE the remove — decision D-50; on Windows `os.remove` on an open handle raises PermissionError which the best-effort clause swallows, so a shape that removes while the fd is open leaves the partial file and is NON-CONFORMING; the state contract (target removed after a failed post-open attempt) is delivered on POSIX and Windows alike; probe appendix/32-rev8-fdclose-probes.py P2/P3; closes adv-c6 F-02 (spec/07-spec-v7.md §4.5 as refreshed by spec/08-spec-v8.md §4.5, QC-2, §11 REQ-010 row) | DECIDED | spec-designer | spec/07-spec-v7.md §4.5 |
| D-49 | The manual dispatch's outcome is NORMATIVE for ALL argv of length 2: `-h`/`--help` in a positional slot are ORDINARY PATH STRINGS — E-READ on the nonexistent `-h` (exit 1, prefixed message, stdout empty), never a help print and never exit 0; v9 REFRESH (adv-c8 F-02/D-52): argparse is now non-conforming OUTRIGHT — the former override-conditions alternative is retracted (spec/09-spec-v9.md §4.1), because an argparse import cannot pass NFR-001's pinned import-set audit and the default help action's stdout-help+exit-0 outcome has no §6.4 matrix row on ANY argv class (live: appendix/30b P4 re-run; appendix/36 P3/P4); closes adv-c6 F-05, tightened by adv-c8 F-02 (spec/09-spec-v9.md §4.1, §6.1 flags row, §8.3 T-C1) | DECIDED | spec-designer | spec/07-spec-v7.md §4.1, §6.1 |
| D-50 | The D-48 except-scoped failure arm CLOSES THE FD BEFORE THE REMOVE: best-effort `fd.close()` (errors ignored) precedes the best-effort `os.remove(path)` in the failure arm — the OS keeps the target's handle open until close runs, and on Windows `os.remove` on an open handle raises PermissionError which the best-effort clause swallows, so a remove-while-open shape leaves the partial file on disk: exactly the D-33/QC-2 outcome the compensation exists to prevent, deterministically, on a supported platform; close-before-remove makes the remove a real step on POSIX and Windows alike, so QC-2's compensation clause stays UNSCOPED (no platform qualifier, no Windows risk row); a shape that removes while the fd is open is NON-CONFORMING; closes SR6-F-01 (probe appendix/32-rev8-fdclose-probes.py: P2 fd.closed True at remove time; P3 remove-after-close ordering in the failure arm; pre-close shape leaves fd open at raise) (spec/08-spec-v8.md §4.5 reference shape, §4.5 compensation bullet, §4.5 table rows 10/11, §8.3 T-C8 note, QC-2, §11 REQ-010 row) | DECIDED | spec-designer | spec/08-spec-v8.md §4.5, QC-2 |
| D-51 | KeyboardInterrupt (SIGINT) striking the write stage is INSIDE the D-48/D-50 compensation contract: the §4.5 failure arm is BaseException-scoped precisely so the signal class is compensated — fd closed (D-50, errors ignored), partial target removed best-effort, then the KI re-raises and exits outside the §6.4 two-valued matrix (shell signal exit 130; REQ-007's own-reporting scope does not extend to the interpreter's Ctrl-C behavior, per §6.4's v9 signal note) — so an interrupted mid-write run leaves NO partial output file; the except-Exception build that §7.3's former unqualified pass-through sentence could be read to sanction is NON-CONFORMING; §7.1's timeout-cancellation residue ("leaves whatever partial output existed at kill time") is scoped to UNCATALOGED kills (SIGKILL, SIGTERM-default) only; closes adv-c8 F-01 = SR7-F-02 (probe evidence: appendix/36-rev9-ki-argparse-probes.py P1 — KI inside the spec's own §4.5 fenced shape removes the target and propagates; P2 — the except-Exception control leaves it, the forbidden divergence) (spec/09-spec-v9.md §4.5 compensation bullet, §4.5 table row 9, §6.4 signal note, §7.1 timeout-cancellation clause, §7.3, §8.3 T-C8 KI sub-case, QC-2 Scope/Mechanism/Verification) | DECIDED | spec-designer | spec/09-spec-v9.md §4.5, §6.4, §7.1, §7.3, QC-2 |
| D-52 | The CLI dispatch has ONE conforming shape: the manual `len(argv) != 2` branch. The former hypothetical argparse alternative (sanctioned under override conditions by §4.1/D-41 since v1) is RETRACTED — an argparse import flunks §9 NFR-001's pinned import-set audit (`csv, io, json, os, sys`), and its builtin help action prints help to STDOUT with exit 0 on the argc==1 class (`csv2json.py -h`), violating NFR-004 with no §6.4 matrix row (the old help-override clause scoped itself to "this two-positional form" and never reached argc==1/3); D-41 (manual argc dispatch) and D-49 (length-2 normative outcome) keep their substance and are refreshed accordingly; closes adv-c8 F-02 (probe evidence: appendix/36-rev9-ki-argparse-probes.py P3 — argc==1 `-h` → usage line on stderr, exit 1, stdout empty; P4 — argc==2 `-h` positional → E-READ, exit 1; adv-c8 report appendix/33-adv-c8.md probes P3a/P3b) (spec/09-spec-v9.md §4.1, §6.1 flags row, §8.3 T-C1, §9 NFR-001 row, §11 REQ-001 row) | DECIDED | spec-designer | spec/09-spec-v9.md §4.1, §6.1, §9, §11 |
| D-53 | The D-51 compensation outcome is a SINGLE-KEYBOARDINTERRUPT contract, conditional on the failure arm running to completion: one KI raised inside the §4.5 try AFTER a successful open runs the D-48/D-50 arm (close per D-50, best-effort remove, re-raise) and leaves NO partial target — but a SECOND KeyboardInterrupt (or any exception from the arm's own close) landing INSIDE the failure arm interrupts the compensation itself (KI is raisable at any bytecode boundary, including inside `fd.close()` and `os.remove`), so the arm's own `except OSError` clauses do not catch it and `os.remove` may never run: the partial file SURVIVES. This residue is recorded as accepted-risk R-5 (§10.1) — the accepted residue of best-effort cleanup, same class as R-1 — NOT contracted away: a KI-resistant arm (signal blocking around the compensation) is rejected because the required `signal` import conflicts with NFR-001's pinned import set (D-52's own precedent: an extra top-level import has no conforming reading). All sites that stated the D-51 outcome ABSOLUTELY are re-scoped: §4.5 compensation bullet + reference shape note, §4.5 mutation row 9, §6.4 signal note, §7.1 timeout-cancellation clause, §7.3, QC-2 Scope/Mechanism/Verification, T-C8's KI sub-case (adds the double-SIGINT residue sentence); closes adv-c9 F-01 (probe evidence: appendix/39b-adv-c9-probes.py P1a/P1b live — double-SIGINT leaves a 1546-of-3092-byte partial target; control P1c single-KI removes it, D-51's mechanism intact when the arm completes) (spec/10-spec-v10.md §4.5, §6.4, §7.1, §7.3, §10.1 R-5, T-C8, QC-2) | DECIDED | spec-designer | spec/10-spec-v10.md §4.5, §6.4, §7.1, §7.3, §10.1 |
| D-54 | KI-AT-OPEN RULE: a KeyboardInterrupt raised BY the `open()` call itself — including the state where the kernel has already applied O_CREAT|O_TRUNC but the signal struck before `open()` returned and `fd` was bound — is classified as an AT-OPEN failure, NOT a D-51 post-open failure: the reference shape observes `fd is None`, so the D-48 arm runs NO compensation and the KI propagates uncompensated. The physical effect (the target may already be truncated to 0 bytes by the kernel's O_TRUNC) is recorded as accepted-risk R-6 (§10.1) — the pre-existing target can be destroyed (left 0-byte) by an interrupted open on a slow/blocking target (NFS, cold FUSE, FIFO); QC-2's wording is scoped accordingly: its "never created or truncated on any failed run" claim holds for EVERY exception class EXCEPT the two recorded residues (R-5 double-KI, R-6 KI-at-open) and the UNCATALOGED kills (SIGKILL/SIGTERM-default, already out of §7.1's scope). The alternative reading (treat KI-from-open as D-51's post-open window because truncation already happened) is rejected as unimplementable: whether the kernel applied O_TRUNC is unobservable from Python without extra syscalls or imports, and the fd-binding point is the only observable boundary the reference shape has. Glossary "successful open (compensation trigger basis)" and §4.5/D-46's at-open story are restated on this explicit signal-timing boundary; §7.1's "survives IFF the failure struck before the open" gains the R-6 exception; T-C8's matrix documents the KI-at-open outcome per this reading; closes adv-c9 F-02 (probe evidence: appendix/39b-adv-c9-probes.py P2a live — SIGINT while blocked in `open()` on a FIFO makes `open()` itself raise KeyboardInterrupt (KI-FROM-OPEN, fd never bound); P2b — reference shape with fd None runs no remove, prior-good target left at 0 bytes) (spec/10-spec-v10.md §4.5, §6.4, §7.1, §10.1 R-6, §12 glossary, T-C8, QC-2) | DECIDED | spec-designer | spec/10-spec-v10.md §4.5, §7.1, §10.1, §12 |
| D-55 | NON-REGULAR OUTPUT PATHS: the §6.4 success row and NFR-004's stdout/stderr rows scope to REGULAR-FILE output paths; when the output path is a character device or other non-regular file openable for writing (`/dev/stdout`, `/dev/stderr`, `/dev/null`, `/dev/fd/N`), the conforming build opens, writes, flushes, closes it and exits 0, and the document appears on that device — this is the documented consequence of the caller's own redirection choice (the POSIX-idiomatic result the caller asked for), NOT a channel-discipline violation. Forbidding non-regular targets is rejected: it needs a new error class outside the CLOSED §6.3 catalog (D-42) plus stat machinery no REQ mandates (same rationale as R-4's record-don't-guard disposition). T-K3's stdout-empty assertion is scoped to regular-file output paths accordingly; the §6.4 success row gains the scope note; closes adv-c9 F-03 (probe evidence: appendix/39b-adv-c9-probes.py P3a/P3b live — output `/dev/stdout` → exit 0 with the JSON document on stdout; `/dev/stderr` → exit 0 with the document on stderr, on a build implementing §4.5's exact reference shape) (spec/10-spec-v10.md §6.1 form row, §6.4 success row, §9 NFR-004 row, §8.2 T-K3, §11 NFR-004 row, plus the §6.1 stderr row and the §12 glossary "silent success" row (both added at v11 per adv-c10 F-02)) | DECIDED | spec-designer | spec/10-spec-v10.md §6.4, §9, §8.2, §11 |
| D-56 | RESIDUE-BOUND FOLDS for the two recorded KI-window residues (no new mechanism, no new residue — the windows and their records are unchanged; only absolute claims and one mis-scoped bound are corrected): (a) D-53's arm-abort class is ANY non-OSError, not only a second KI — R-5's own wording already reads "(or any non-OSError)" — so a SECOND MemoryError landing inside the §4.5 failure arm (at its `fd.close()` or `os.remove`, or at any allocation the arm performs; the OOM condition does not lift while the arm runs under the very RLIMIT_AS vehicle T-C16 mandates) aborts the compensation exactly like a second KI: `os.remove` never runs and the partial file SURVIVES while the E-MEM write-phase message `csv2json: error: out of memory writing <out>` is still what the run reports. The five absolute write-phase-removal claims are folded to carry the D-53/R-5 qualifier: §5.3 S-14(e) ("the file is GONE"), §6.3's E-MEM row ("no partial file survives"), §7.2's footprint sentence ("the target removed"), §8.3 T-C16 ("no conforming mechanism can leave it present" plus its stateless-form sentence), QC-2 Verification (write-phase path-absent assertion), and §4.5's normative-contract lead sentence — closes adv-c10 F-01 (probe evidence: appendix/47-rev11-adv10-folds-probes.py P1a live — MemoryError at `fd.write` plus a second MemoryError at the arm's `fd.close()` leaves the partial file PRESENT (1546/3092 bytes) with exactly the E-MEM write-phase stderr line; control P1b — single MemoryError, arm completes, partial REMOVED (D-46 trigger + D-50 ordering intact); P1c honest negative — a pure RLIMIT_AS sweep did not reproduce the cascade (the arm's sub-KB allocations are freelist hits after a mid-write OOM), so the fold rests on the sanctioned interruption points plus the textual contradiction, the same evidence class the board accepted for D-53/R-5 in appendix/39b P1a/P1b); (b) R-6's residue bound is WIDENED from "bounded to pre-existing targets" to BOTH flavors of the same KI-at-open window — a PRE-EXISTING target may be left truncated to 0 bytes (kernel O_TRUNC), and an ABSENT target may be left CREATED at 0 bytes (kernel O_CREAT, signal before `fd` binds, arm sees `fd is None`, no compensation, exit via the signal path); §10.1 R-6 (body + Impact), QC-2 Scope's exception enumeration, §4.5's KI-AT-OPEN paragraph, §7.2's footprint sentence, and the §11 D-54 index entry carry the create flavor — closes adv-c10 F-04 (probe evidence: appendix/47 P4 textual bound check — the create flavor is now named at all five mirrored sites; the mechanism is identical to appendix/39b P2b with the absent-path precondition) (spec/11-spec-v11.md §4.5, §5.3 S-14(e), §6.3 E-MEM, §7.1, §7.2, §8.3 T-C16, §10.1 R-5/R-6, QC-2, §11 D-53/D-54 index entries) | DECIDED | spec-designer | spec/11-spec-v11.md §4.5, §5.3, §6.3, §7.1, §7.2, §8.3, §10.1, QC-2, §11 |
| D-57 | AT-OPEN MEMORYERROR RULE: a MemoryError raised BY the `open()` call itself — the kernel has already applied O_CREAT|O_TRUNC, CPython's DECREF cleanup closes the raw fd, and the wrapper raises before `fd` binds — is classified by the SAME fd-binding observable as D-54's KI-at-open class: the §4.5 reference shape observes `fd is None`, the D-48 arm runs NO compensation, the run reports E-MEM's write-phase form (`out of memory writing <out>`, exit 1) via main's residual net, and the target may be left 0-byte — an ABSENT target CREATED or a PRE-EXISTING target truncated (both flavors of the same window; the kernel-level state is identical to the KI-at-open case). R-6's trigger is widened from "KI" to "KI or MemoryError at open" (same record, both flavors, §10.1); the "byte-untouched" at-open clause is scoped to the OSError at-open forms (D-46 unchanged for OSError); T-C16's "no conforming mechanism can otherwise leave it present" sentence gains the at-open carve-out (an at-open failure never ran the compensation — its residue is the R-6/D-57 class, not that sentence's concern); §5.1 gains the at-open MemoryError edge and its pre-open encode edge is reworded to "output path untouched". Classification alternative rejected: contracting a D-33 compensation trigger for at-open MemoryError has no conforming mechanism (whether the kernel applied O_CREAT|O_TRUNC is unobservable from Python — the same fd-binding rationale as D-54, which the reviewer identified as applying verbatim). closes adv-c11 F-01 (P1) and F-04 (P3, the §5.1 edge) (probe evidence: appendix/51-rev12-adv11-folds-probes.py B1 — absent target CREATED 0-byte, B2 — pre-existing target TRUNCATED 0-byte, both with the E-MEM write-phase stderr line and exit 1, reproducing the reviewer's appendix/48b P2a/P2b on the identical fault) (spec/12-spec-v12.md §4.5, §4.5 mutation rows 3/6/7/9/10/11/12/13, §5.1, §5.3 S-14(f), §6.3, §6.4, §7.1, §7.2, §7.3, §8.3, §8.4, QC-2, §10.1 R-6, §11, §12) | DECIDED | spec-designer | spec/12-spec-v12.md §4.5, §5.1, §10.1, QC-2, §12 |
| D-58 | CONFORMING FUSION latitude for the per-record scan (behavior-neutral): the §4.3.3 FSM walk and the §4.3.2 break count may be computed in ONE fused pass — a single scan of `record_text` that advances the counter exactly where the normative D-28 collapse rule advances it, transitions the FSM exactly where the §4.3.3 table transitions it, and remembers the opening line from that same counter AT EVERY FIELD_START→QUOTED transition (the table's row — the remembered line on a record ending QUOTED is the UNCLOSED field's opening quote, exactly what S-10/T-U3/T-C7 pin as M) — outcome-identical to the two-quantity form (state at end of span, opening line M, per-record break count); neither form is required, either is conforming, NO behavior change (D-38/§4.2's decode-stage counting and `count_line_breaks` as a decode helper are unchanged; the latitude is scoped to the per-record scan). Rationale (v14 re-based per D-59): the form latitude exists because the per-record Python-level scan dominates the NFR-003 envelope budget on the reference hardware class, and the FUSED form stays ahead of the two-quantity form at EITHER CPython name binding (1.29x module-bound, 1.64x function-bound — binding-controlled, appendix/66-rev14-binding-timing.py, run twice); the earlier single-binding rationale ("the literal two-pass walk consumed 27.3 s of the 30 s envelope ... the fused walk measured 9.1 s, leaving roughly 20 s" — cross-artifact, module-bound vs function-bound) misattributed CPython name-binding cost to scan form and is RETRACTED; the "~3-5 s margin" corollary is retracted with it (no contract depends on a per-stage margin; T-C9 stays a diagnostic envelope spot check). T-C9/QC-5 name the REFERENCE HARDWARE CLASS for the 30 s figure — a single-core general-purpose x86-64 or ARM64 SBC-class machine with the payload already in memory — and the spot check stays diagnostic, not a gate (slower/throttled hosts may exceed 30 s without any contract failure). closes adv-c11 F-02 (P2); F-02's outcome-identity evidence re-based in v14 (adv-c13 F-02) and RE-AIMED in v15 to the real shape-vs-shape battery (adv-c14 F-01): the live identity probe is appendix/77-rev15-shape-identity.py — it builds BOTH shapes (two-quantity table-latch FSM + separate break pass vs fused single pass) and asserts full per-record outcome identity AND both shapes' derivation of the normative (N, M) over a 13-corpus family (the six S-10/T-C7 corpora plus seven discriminators incl. a re-open-on-a-later-record-relative-line corpus that discriminates a re-remembering build M=3 from the spec's no-re-remember latch M=2; appendix/66 Part B's identity check under this claim was a self-comparison — `tq` and `fu` were the same call — and 77's T1/T2 pins that defect; 66 Part B's normative-N/M assertions remain valid and cited); appendix/51 B3 remains cited ONLY for per-record break-count and end-state identity between the shapes (its shared first-quote latch computes M=2 where the table computes M=3 — the probe demonstrates this; T-U3/T-C7 are the M authority); timing evidence appendix/66-rev14-binding-timing.py (D-59's binding-controlled set; historical single-regime artifacts appendix/48c/55h each reproduce their own regime, cross-comparison void; v13: the row's earlier "fused ~0.8-1 s / leaves the envelope ample" wording corrected per SR11-F-01, v14: the corrected numbers' cross-artifact comparison re-based per adv-c13 F-01/D-59) | DECIDED | spec-designer | spec/15-spec-v15.md §4.3.2/§4.3.3 counting-rule paragraph, §8.3 T-C9, §9 NFR-003 row, QC-5, §11 NFR-003 row |
| D-59 | BINDING-CONTROLLED PERFORMANCE EVIDENCE RULE (evidence-integrity, no mechanism change): every stage-cost number the spec cites as NFR-003 evidence MUST come from a measurement whose CPython name binding (module-level globals vs function-local fast locals) is stated in the same sentence, and form comparisons (two-quantity vs D-58 fused) are stated ONLY within one binding — cross-binding comparison of per-stage numbers is VOID, because the binding effect (measured ~1.7x on the reference class) exceeds the form effect (~1.3-1.6x) and misattributing it is the adv-c13 F-01 defect class. The sanctioned evidence artifact is appendix/66-rev14-binding-timing.py (one process measures BOTH forms under BOTH bindings plus the reader-only and dict+serialize baselines on the 55 MB / 250k-row payload; run twice 2026-09-20: two-quantity 25.7 s module-bound / 14.9 s function-bound, re-run 25.3/14.9; fused 19.9 s module-bound / 9.1 s function-bound, re-run 19.5/9.1; reader-only 0.8 s; dict+serialize 0.4 s; four-cell result agreement guard). Consequences carried by this decision: (a) the v13 margin narratives are RETRACTED — "fused leaves roughly 20 s" and "two-quantity leaves only ~3-5 s" mixed regimes and no contract depends on any per-stage margin (T-C9 remains a diagnostic envelope spot check asserting < 30 s / < 1 GB RSS); (b) appendix/48c and appendix/55h remain cited as HISTORICAL single-regime measurements (module-bound and function-bound respectively) whose own-regime figures reproduce but whose cross-comparison is void; (c) no conforming build is constrained by any of these numbers — they are diagnostic evidence for the envelope, not gates. closes adv-c13 F-01 (P1) (probe evidence: appendix/66-rev14-binding-timing.py A-series, 27/27 PASS twice; the binding root cause was demonstrated by the reviewer's appendix/62d-adv-c13-globals.py and appendix/62e-adv-c13-fusedmodule.py); v15 additions: the §4.3.2 note named in this row's site list actually exists as of v15 (adv-c14 F-04 = SR13-F-02 — a phantom mirror until the one-sentence D-59 mirror was written at §4.3.2's D-28 counter paragraph), and the reader-only/dict+serialize baselines now carry their module-bound labels at §8.3 T-C9/QC-5 (adv-c14 F-05 — D-59's own same-sentence rule applied to its baselines) | DECIDED | spec-designer | spec/15-spec-v15.md §8.3 T-C9, QC-5 Verification, §9 NFR-003 row, §11 NFR-003 row, §4.3.2 note |
